controls.regle: Asynchronous integrations (message queues, event notifications, deferred tasks) are designed to be received multiple times without duplicate effects (idempotence), with a bounded retry policy and a dead-letter queue dedicated to repeated failures.
controls.verification: Verify the presence of a unique message identifier guaranteeing deduplication, the configuration of a bounded retry policy (delay, maximum number of attempts), and the activation of a dead-letter queue for repeatedly failing messages.
controls.preuve_attendue: Retry policy configuration (delay, max attempts) + dead-letter queue configuration + example of a message replay without duplicate effect.
controls.grille_verdict: compliant = idempotence demonstrated + bounded retry + active dead-letter queue ; partial = idempotence demonstrated without a dead-letter queue ; non-compliant = no idempotence guarantee observed
actions_audit: Verify the presence of a unique message identifier and the deduplication mechanism for each asynchronous integration; attach the configuration excerpts.
Replay a duplicate message in a test environment and confirm the absence of a duplicated business effect; document the result.
If a gap is found: design the missing idempotence and activate a bounded dead-letter queue.
standards: EIP — Enterprise Integration Patterns (Idempotent Receiver, Dead Letter Channel)

controls.regle: Consumed external dependencies (third-party APIs, AI inference models, shared services) are subject to known, documented, and monitored quotas and rate thresholds, with a controlled degradation plan in case of overrun.
controls.verification: Inventory the consumed external dependencies and their contractual quotas (TPM/RPM, calls/minute); verify that observed usage stays under the declared thresholds and that a degradation plan (queueing, fallback, controlled error message) exists in case of overrun.
controls.preuve_attendue: Inventory of external dependencies with contractual quotas + observed usage over the period + documented degradation plan.
controls.grille_verdict: compliant = quotas known, usage under threshold, degradation plan tested ; partial = quotas known without a degradation plan ; non-compliant = quotas unknown or overruns not controlled
actions_audit: Inventory the consumed external dependencies and their contractual quotas; attach the inventory and observed usage.
Simulate or observe a quota overrun and verify the degradation behavior; document the result.
If a gap is found: negotiate/document the missing quotas and implement a degradation plan.
standards: Site Reliability Engineering (Google) — gestion de la charge

controls.regle: Latency targets (p50/p95/p99) are declared for each critical journey and continuously measured under real conditions, with systematic comparison to the declared target.
controls.verification: Verify the existence of declared latency targets per critical journey and the presence of p50/p95/p99 metrics measured over a representative period (7-30 days); compare the measurements to the declared targets.
controls.preuve_attendue: Document of latency targets per journey + export of p50/p95/p99 metrics measured over the period.
controls.grille_verdict: compliant = targets declared and measurements compliant over the period ; partial = measurements available without a declared target (or vice versa) ; non-compliant = neither target nor measurement available
actions_audit: Extract the p50/p95/p99 latency metrics over a representative period for each critical journey; attach the export.
Compare the measurements to the declared targets; document any observed gaps.
If a gap is found: declare the missing targets or instrument the unmeasured journeys.

controls.regle: Load tests representative of the target are run regularly, at minimum before every major production release, with performance budgets defined and verified in continuous integration, blocking any significant regression.
controls.verification: Look for the load test scripts (k6, Locust, JMeter, or equivalent) and their execution in CI; verify the existence of performance thresholds (budgets) and the pipeline's behavior in case of overrun.
controls.preuve_attendue: Report of the latest load test + performance budget configuration in CI + evidence of a pipeline failure on budget overrun.
controls.grille_verdict: compliant = regular load tests + active blocking budgets ; partial = regular load tests without a blocking budget ; non-compliant = no load test observed
actions_audit: Look for the load test scripts and execution history; attach the latest report.
Verify the performance budget configuration in CI and trigger a regression test to confirm the blocking behavior; document the result.
If a gap is found: implement the missing load tests and blocking budgets.
standards: ISO/IEC 25010:2011 — Efficacité de performance (utilisation des ressources)
DORA (Accelerate) — pratiques de test en continu

controls.regle: A caching strategy is defined and applied to the identified contention points (costly responses, recurring calls to external dependencies), with an explicit invalidation policy.
controls.verification: Identify the contention points (latency, cost, load) on the main journeys and verify the presence of a suitable caching mechanism (application, HTTP, semantic) with a documented invalidation policy.
controls.preuve_attendue: Cache configuration (TTL, key, scope) + justification of the contention points covered.
controls.grille_verdict: compliant = cache in place on the major contention points with controlled invalidation ; partial = partial cache or uncontrolled invalidation ; non-compliant = no cache despite identified contention points
actions_audit: Identify the contention points (latency, cost, load) on the main journeys; attach the analysis.
Verify the cache configuration and its invalidation policy at these points; document the coverage.
If a gap is found: implement the missing cache and define the invalidation policy.
standards: ISO/IEC 25010:2011 — Efficacité de performance (utilisation des ressources)

controls.regle: Every endpoint returning a collection applies systematic pagination with a bounded page size, avoiding any uncontrolled payload.
controls.verification: Inventory the endpoints returning collections; verify the presence of pagination (cursor or offset/limit) and a bounded maximum page size for each.
controls.preuve_attendue: List of collection endpoints with pagination parameters + example of a full, non-paginated payload response (if applicable).
controls.grille_verdict: compliant = systematic and bounded pagination on 100% of collection endpoints ; partial = partial pagination ; non-compliant = endpoints returning unbounded collections
actions_audit: Inventory the endpoints returning collections; attach the list with pagination parameters.
Query an endpoint without a pagination parameter and confirm the presence of a default bound; document the result.
If a gap is found: instrument the missing pagination and bound the page size.

controls.regle: Connections to stateful dependent services (database, cache, third-party services) are managed by a properly sized and configured connection pool, avoiding any connection exhaustion under load.
controls.verification: Verify the connection pooling configuration (min/max size, timeout) for each stateful dependency, and the absence of a connection opened per request.
controls.preuve_attendue: Connection pool configuration per dependency + pool usage metrics under load.
controls.grille_verdict: compliant = pooling configured and sized for all stateful dependencies ; partial = partial pooling ; non-compliant = non-pooled connections (opened per request)
actions_audit: Inventory the stateful dependencies (database, cache, third-party services) and their pooling configuration; attach the inventory.
Observe the pool usage metrics under load (saturation, wait time); document the result.
If a gap is found: configure the missing pooling and size it according to the target load.
standards: ISO/IEC 25010:2011 — Efficacité de performance (utilisation des ressources)

controls.regle: The horizontal and/or vertical scaling capacity is documented (chosen mechanism, known limits) and validated by a test representative of the target load.
controls.verification: Verify the documentation of the scalability mechanism (horizontal autoscaling, vertical scale-up) and the existence of a test that validated the declared target load.
controls.preuve_attendue: Scalability strategy documentation + target load test report + autoscaling configuration.
controls.grille_verdict: compliant = scalability documented and validated by a test at target ; partial = documented without test validation ; non-compliant = scalability not documented
actions_audit: Request the documentation of the scalability mechanism (horizontal/vertical) and its known limits; attach the document.
Verify the load test report that validated the declared target; document the result.
If a gap is found: document the mechanism and conduct the missing target validation test.
